item.title: BRICS opens up new possibilities for more dynamic Global South
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BEIJING, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- When the BRICS cooperation mechanism was formally launched in 2006, it opened a new chapter for cooperation among major emerging economies. Two decades on, BRICS has, through the ebbs and flows of the global economy, expanded through multiple rounds of enlargement and broadened the scope of its cooperation.
This evolution has ushered in a new era of greater BRICS cooperation, better reflecting the growing weight and aspirations of the Global South.
When BRICS leaders prepare to gather for this year's summit in New Delhi, India, the mechanism is playing a greater role in amplifying the collective voice of emerging economies, and expanding practical cooperation amid a changing international landscape beset by raging protectionism and economic fragmentation.
Its growing weight is reflected in its economic and demographic scale. BRICS countries now account for approximately 40 percent of global GDP at purchasing power parity and nearly half of the world's population. Data released by the UN Trade and Development in March showed that the intra-BRICS merchandise trade has expanded more than 13-fold since 2003, and exports reached 1.17 trillion U.S. dollars in 2024.
BRICS, however, is more than an economic force. Its growing significance lies in how countries with different development paths are pooling their strengths in resources, industry and technology to advance shared development.
A prominent area is financing. For many developing economies, access to affordable, long-term funding remains critical to turning development ambitions into reality. The New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai, has helped provide such an option by mobilizing resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects. Figures released by the bank showed that by the end of the first quarter of 2026, the NDB had approved 42.9 billion dollars in financing for 140 projects.
Covering such areas as infrastructure, clean energy and digital transformation, these projects address the pressing development needs of Global South countries while echoing the priorities highlighted by the theme of the forthcoming BRICS Summit, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability."
The ever-evolving BRICS cooperation is also helping developing countries gain new growth momentum. In recent years, BRICS cooperation has been expanding into areas like renewable energy, digital infrastructure, scientific and technological innovation.
A case in point is the BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution Innovation Center in Xiamen, which was established in 2020 to provide a platform for cooperation in digitalization, advanced manufacturing and technological innovation.
These efforts point to the broader value of BRICS: it is not simply giving the Global South a stronger voice, but creating practical opportunities for countries to access financing, technology and cooperation suited to their development needs.
Such collaboration helps explain BRICS' growing appeal to countries seeking greater opportunities to participate and cooperate. As a founding member, China has contributed not only by building platforms for practical cooperation, but also by supporting greater openness and broader participation to promote high-quality cooperation within an expanded BRICS.
Some in the West portray BRICS as a rival bloc seeking to build a parallel order. Yet this claim bears little resemblance to reality. BRICS stands for openness, inclusiveness and mutual benefit, not confrontation or exclusion. That is fundamentally different from the exclusive blocs championed by some Western countries, and a key reason behind the growing vitality of BRICS.
Looking ahead, BRICS is poised to embark on its third "golden decade" after 20 years of growth and transformation. By rising up to the challenges of the times, BRICS countries can help shape a more equal and orderly multipolar world and a more universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and, in doing so, write a new chapter of solidarity and cooperation across the Global South.

item.title: China, India are making arrangements for Xi-Modi meeting, says spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- China and India are making arrangements for a meeting between President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the upcoming 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Friday.
This will mark the third consecutive year in which Xi and Modi meet, following their meetings in Kazan and Tianjin, said Mao Ning, the spokesperson, at a regular news briefing.
She said China stands ready to work with India to follow the strategic guidance of the two leaders, view bilateral relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, strengthen communication, expand cooperation, and properly handle differences, so as to be good-neighborly friends and partners helping each other succeed.

item.title: Xi leaves for 18th BRICS Summit in India
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-12
BEIJING, Sept. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping left Beijing on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi at the invitation of Prime Minister of the Republic of India Narendra Modi.
Xi's entourage includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee, and Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese foreign minister.

item.title: Beyond classrooms: Xi inspires teachers to nurture talent for national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
A volunteer teacher (C) runs with students in the morning at the primary school of Sheyit Village in Karajol Township under Artux City, Kizilsu Kirgiz Autonomous Prefecture, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, April 24, 2025. (Xinhua/Xu Hongyan)
BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- As millions of teachers across China celebrated Teachers' Day on Thursday, they received a familiar message of greetings from President Xi Jinping.
In a congratulatory message released a day earlier, Xi commended teachers nationwide for dedicating themselves to education, imparting knowledge and nurturing young minds, highlighting their significant contributions to the country's development.
He called on teachers to enhance their professional competence and capabilities, and foster a new generation of young people to shoulder the mission of realizing national rejuvenation.
Xi also called for greater respect for educators, stronger support for education, and concerted efforts to make China a leading country in education.
As an inspiring move, the central authorities on Thursday honored 25 teachers from across the country for their outstanding work.
RESPECT FOR TEACHERS
Grounded in the legacies of Confucius and Mencius, reverence for teachers has deep roots in Chinese culture and remains an important value in Chinese society today.
Xi himself has long held the teaching profession in high regard. He once invoked a well-known Chinese saying to capture the profession's significance: "A stick of chalk and a modest podium shape the fate of a nation."
In Xi's view, good educators are expected to possess ideals and convictions, moral integrity, knowledge and benevolence.
His bond with teachers was forged during his school years and has endured ever since.
On the eve of Teachers' Day in 2016, Xi returned to his alma mater, Beijing Bayi School. Seeing his former teachers again, he slowed his pace and held their hands firmly. When addressed as "leader," he demurred: "Here, there are no leaders. Everyone is a student."
Among the teachers was Chen Qiuying, Xi's Chinese teacher and a guide to the world of poetry during his teenage years. For decades thereafter, they remained in touch.
"He would often bring me books over the years," Chen recalled. "Some were his doctoral dissertation or his own works, while others introduced the places where he had recently taken up a new post. Sometimes, he would even send me a few bulbs of Fujian narcissus in the depths of winter."
Xi's respect for teachers goes beyond ceremonial recognition. He has repeatedly called for greater support for teachers, particularly those working in rural areas, by improving their pay, working conditions and social standing.
With his support, China issued a policy document dedicated to rural teachers and took actions to ensure that the average income of primary and secondary school teachers nationwide was on par with or higher than that of local civil servants.
A teacher guides children in performing a dragon dance at a childcare center in Luzhou City, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Sept. 5, 2025. (Xinhua/Jiang Hongjing)
MAKING TEACHERS AND EDUCATION A PRIORITY
From his grassroots posts to the nation's top leadership, Xi has consistently made teachers and education a governance priority.
He has visited schools and campuses to learn about teachers' work and living conditions, discussed education issues with national legislators and political advisors, and supported paired-assistance programs designed to improve education quality in less-developed regions.
For a vast and populous country facing uneven distribution of educational resources, Xi has stressed the need to further expand access to quality basic education and promote educational fairness, emphasizing education's role in promoting greater social equity.
In June 2024, Xi visited an ethnic middle school in Qinghai, a less-developed province in northwest China, where he encouraged teachers to help children grow and thrive.
Funded and supported by Shanghai, the school opened in 2019 to meet the pressing need for quality secondary education among children from pastoral communities on the plateau.
Zhou Quan, a Shanghai teacher who taught at the school through the paired-assistance program, was delighted to learn that many of his students there gained admission to leading universities upon graduation.
"Helping them build confidence, broaden their horizons and achieve their academic goals has been the most rewarding part of my career," said the chemistry teacher.
As AI reshapes education, Xi has emphasized the importance of advancing digital education to make quality educational resources more accessible to students, regardless of where they live.
Efforts to expand access to education have also benefited students with disabilities. In recent years, about 30,000 students with disabilities have entered higher education each year.
Xi has envisioned vocational education in China shifting gears to help more children fulfill their potential. The country now boasts the world's largest vocational education system, with more than 10 million annual graduates.
A little-known fact is that Xi also served as president of a vocational school in Fuzhou for six years in the 1990s, during his tenure as Party chief of the coastal city. He played an active role in the school's development, now known as Minjiang University, championing causes such as enrolling an armless student -- a pioneering move in Fujian Province at the time.
Wu Yuanzhou instructs students in practice at the bricklaying training base of Tianjin Railway Technical and Vocational College in Tianjin, north China, Sept. 9, 2025. (Xinhua/Li Ran)
TOWARD A GLOBAL LEADER IN EDUCATION
China has set sights on becoming a global leader in education by 2035 -- an endeavor fueling its pursuit of modernization and national rejuvenation.
The country boasts the world's largest education system, with roughly 440,000 schools at all levels and of all types, 280 million students, and 18.7 million teachers.
China has made significant progress toward that goal. According to Education Minister Huai Jinpeng, the country's overall level of education modernization now ranks among the upper-middle tier globally. In basic education, coverage and key indicators had surpassed the average levels of upper-middle-income countries, with preschool and compulsory education reaching the average levels of high-income countries.
On the higher education front, 55 million graduates entered the workforce and broader society over the five years leading up to 2025. Meanwhile, vocational education supplied more than 70 percent of the newly added highly skilled workers for modern industries, helping support the country's comprehensive modern industrial system.
Xi regards strengthening the teaching workforce as the most important fundamental work for building China into a leading country in education.
To this end, China plans to launch a national initiative on teacher development, accompanied by integrated reforms in teacher preparation, professional development, management and support in the coming years.
The emphasis on teachers also reflects Xi's broader vision of education -- cultivating the talent needed to drive scientific and technological progress and strengthen the country's capacity for innovation.
In a reply letter in June 2024, he encouraged Andrew Chi-Chih Yao, a Turing Award laureate and professor at Tsinghua University, to explore new approaches to nurturing innovative talent, fostering interdisciplinary work and advancing frontier research.
"Today's students are the major driving force that will realize our great Chinese dream: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," Xi once remarked. "Teachers are dream builders, undertaking their mission to forge a 'dream team.'"

item.title: Death toll rises to 25 after cargo ship fire in east China's Qingdao
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
This photo taken on Sept. 10, 2026 shows the site of a cargo ship fire in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province. (Xinhua/Li Aoqiu)
QINGDAO, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- The death toll from the foreign cargo ship which caught fire at a shipyard in Qingdao, east China's Shandong Province, has risen to 25, local authorities said Thursday evening.
Rescuers have located all 25 individuals initially reported missing, but none showed signs of life.
The fire broke out at around 11:15 a.m. when the ship was undergoing maintenance at China State Shipbuilding Corporation Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding Co., Ltd., according to the municipal fire and rescue bureau.
A total of 42 people were aboard the ship. Twelve were safely evacuated, and five injured individuals were taken to the hospital, where they are in stable condition.
The blaze was extinguished at around 2:30 p.m.
Emergency management, fire and rescue, police, and medical departments were immediately mobilized to carry out search and rescue operations following the incident.

item.title: Xi to attend New Delhi summit to boost greater BRICS cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
* "It is for our shared pursuit and for the overarching trend of peace and development that we BRICS countries have come together," Chinese President Xi Jinping has said.
* Today, the BRICS has expanded to 11 member countries and 10 partner countries, becoming a force for advancing a multipolar world and greater democracy in international relations.
BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi from Sept. 12 to 13, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Thursday.
Over the past two decades, BRICS has grown into a major platform for cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries, with an ever-expanding role in global affairs.
China, as a staunch supporter and active participant in BRICS, has consistently upheld the BRICS Spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation, working with its partners to turn shared aspirations into practical cooperation and advance common development.
This photo taken on Aug. 20, 2025 shows a view of the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, India. (Xinhua/Wu Yue)
At the upcoming summit, Xi will join other leaders in charting a new course for the high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation, pooling the collective strength of the Global South and contributing stability and positive momentum to a world undergoing profound changes.
BUILDING STRONGER BRICS
In March 2013, Xi attended the fifth BRICS Summit in Durban, South Africa. It was his first international summit as Chinese president.
"We, the five BRICS countries, come from four different continents. The grand goal of fostering partnership for common development and the noble cause of promoting democracy in international relations and advancing peace and development of mankind have brought us together," he said in a keynote speech at the summit.
Xi called on BRICS countries to move toward the goal of integrated markets, multi-tiered financial network, connectivity by land, air and sea, and greater cultural exchanges.
Two years later, at the seventh BRICS Summit held in Ufa, Russia, Xi called for building a partnership for world peace, common development, inter-civilization dialogue and more effective global economic governance.
When China was the BRICS chair back in 2017, Xi proposed the "BRICS Plus" cooperation model at the ninth BRICS Summit in Xiamen, calling for getting more emerging markets and developing countries involved in the group's concerted endeavors for cooperation and mutual benefits.
In October 2024, the 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia, marked the first BRICS leaders' offline summit since the group's expansion. "It is for our shared pursuit and for the overarching trend of peace and development that we BRICS countries have come together," Xi said in a speech at the summit.
Building on this vision, Xi proposed building a BRICS committed to peace, innovation, green development, justice and closer people-to-people exchanges.
Xi has advanced BRICS cooperation through "highly constructive proposals," bringing more Global South countries that share a vision of a multipolar world into dialogue and practical cooperation, thereby strengthening the appeal and influence of BRICS, said Alexander Gusev, director of Russia's Institute for Strategic Planning and Forecasting.
BRICS countries account for nearly half of the world's population, around 30 percent of the global economy and one-fifth of global trade.
"China seeks the greatest common ground for cooperation through equal dialogue, builds consensus around shared interests, and continuously strengthens the cohesion and capacity for action of BRICS cooperation," said Mohamed Hussein, first deputy head of Egypt's State Information Service.
BRICS is a platform with great potential while strengths and differences among its members are an asset, said Marcos Cordeiro Pires, a professor of political and economic sciences at the Sao Paulo State University.
In a world undergoing profound changes, the BRICS is amplifying the voices of Global South countries in demands for better governance, more security and the right to development, said Pires.
BRICS IN ACTION
At Xiamen Port in southeast China's Fujian Province, a major hub for international shipping, the BRICS Go-Global Express officially kicked off in late July, providing a new bridge for Chinese companies to expand into BRICS markets abroad.
The inaugural event focused on Nigeria, which officially became a BRICS partner country last year. Hassan Mohammed, commissioner of the Trade Division at the Consulate General of Nigeria in Shanghai, said the BRICS Plus framework had created more platforms for exchanges and brought the two countries closer together.
This photo taken on July 29, 2026 shows a view of a quay in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province. (Xinhua/Lin Shanchuan)
At the 12th BRICS Summit in November 2020, Xi announced China's plan to set up a BRICS Partnership on New Industrial Revolution innovation center in Xiamen.
Since its establishment, the center has facilitated more than 100 cooperation projects, with a total investment of over 62 billion yuan (9.24 billion U.S. dollars). It has also launched a scholarship for emerging industries, helping BRICS countries cultivate talent across a range of fields, including industry and communications.
Delivering results has been central to the BRICS agenda. As Xi once put it, "BRICS is not a talking shop, but a task force that gets things done."
By the end of 2025, the New Development Bank, whose establishment Xi personally championed, had approved 139 projects with total financing of about 43 billion dollars, bringing tangible benefits to people in Global South countries through green energy, transport infrastructure and access to clean drinking water.
In 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative at the general debate of the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly. Five years on, the initiative is complementing and reinforcing the BRICS cooperation mechanism, bringing development further to the forefront of the international agenda.
China has since launched initiatives to expand BRICS cooperation in areas including deep-sea resources, the digital economy, green industries and clean energy. It has also proposed new programs in artificial intelligence and digital education.
BRICS and the Global Development Initiative have increasingly complemented and reinforced each other, said Siti Mutiah Setiawati, a lecturer at Gadjah Mada University in Indonesia.
Together, they have brought greater attention to development on the international agenda, and helped translate shared aspirations into practical outcomes for emerging markets and developing countries, she said.
ADVANCING GOVERNANCE REFORM
In September last year, Xi proposed the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization Plus" Meeting in the northern Chinese port city of Tianjin.
Seven days later, when addressing a virtual BRICS Summit, Xi said the GGI "is aimed at galvanizing joint global action for a more just and equitable global governance system."
BRICS countries are increasingly finding common ground on issues ranging from development and a more multipolar world to global governance reform. At the 2024 BRICS Summit, Xi called for building the group into "a vanguard for advancing global governance reform."
The GGI provides an important framework for BRICS to advance global governance reform, helping strengthen the UN-centered international system and make global governance more just, equitable and representative, said B. R. Deepak, professor of Chinese and China Studies at the Centre of Chinese and Southeast Asian Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Aerial photo taken on June 17, 2022 shows the headquarters building of the New Development Bank (NDB), also known as the BRICS bank, in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe)
This vision has also been reflected in Xi's calls for greater cooperation among BRICS countries. At the "BRICS Plus" leaders' dialogue in Kazan, Russia, Xi called on BRICS countries to become the main driving force for common development, play an active and leading role in the global economic governance reform, and make development the core of international economic and trade agenda.
At the BRICS Business Forum in Johannesburg, South Africa, in 2018, Xi also called on BRICS countries to firmly support the multilateral trading regime, advance global economic governance reform and increase the representation and voice of emerging markets and developing countries.
Concrete actions have accompanied these calls on reforming major international financial institutions. BRICS countries have put forward clear positions on reforms of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) quota system and the World Bank's shareholding structure.
The Rio de Janeiro Declaration, adopted at the 17th BRICS Summit held last year in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, stressed that further quota realignment in the IMF should increase the shares of emerging markets and developing economies.
As for the World Bank, the declaration called for "increased voice and representation of developing countries, underpinned by a shareholding realignment that corrects their historic underrepresentation."
"The greatest contribution of BRICS over the last two decades has been its role in changing the conversation about global political governance," said Ronney Ncwadi, professor and director of the School of Economics, Development and Tourism at Nelson Mandela University.
"BRICS has demonstrated that emerging and developing economies are no longer just recipients of global rules, but are increasingly participating in shaping those rules," said Ncwadi.

item.title: From Bishkek to New Delhi, Xi advocates Global South cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-11
Chinese President Xi Jinping attends a group photo session ahead of the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" meeting in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Sept. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Ye)
BEIJING, Sept. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping is heading to New Delhi for this year's BRICS gathering just over a week after he took part in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek.
The two back-to-back multilateral engagements converge on a single, defining theme: galvanizing solidarity and cooperation across the Global South.
Photo taken on Aug. 24, 2017 shows a flowerbed at the Xiamen International Conference and Exhibition Center in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian Province. (Xinhua/Jiang Kehong)
EXPANDING FAMILY
The SCO "takes root in the Global South, its heart beats with the Global South, and it is an important pillar of South-South cooperation," Xi said at the Bishkek summit concluded on Tuesday last week, calling on the SCO to "promote the development and rise of the Global South through the SCO Wisdom."
The Chinese leader is expected to put forward further proposals on Global South cooperation at the upcoming BRICS summit, as he has noted that the BRICS is "standing at the forefront of the Global South."
This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO and the 20th anniversary of the BRICS cooperation mechanism, both milestone occasions.
Riding the wave of the collective rise of the Global South, BRICS and the SCO have over the years expanded their membership and broadened their networks of developing partners. Their members jointly account for more than half of the world's population and about 30 percent of the global economy. This illustrates the fact that the two groupings have evolved into major platforms for Global South cooperation.
Xi has not only joined other leaders of member countries in pushing for their respective expansions, but also put forward new ideas and initiatives like the "BRICS Plus" cooperation approach and the building of an SCO community with a shared future, opening up new vistas for win-win cooperation among Global South countries.
"China has consistently provided a clear vision and momentum for BRICS and the SCO, both conceptually and practically," said Humprey Arnaldo Russel, head of the ASEAN-China Research Center at the University of Indonesia.
"It transformed BRICS from a relatively exclusive grouping into a broader platform for cooperation among developing countries and the wider Global South," he added.
Chinese expert Li Guiqiang (L) gives instructions on vegetable cultivation at the China-Ethiopia Addis Ababa Agricultural Technology Demonstration and Training Center in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on Aug. 20, 2025. (Xinhua/Han Xu)
DEVELOPMENT FIRST
At the SCO summit last week, Xi called on countries to "stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity."
Amid a turbulent and rapidly changing international landscape, development still faces severe challenges, and the road to prosperity for the Global South will not be straight.
"The Global South emerges for development and prospers through development. We should make ourselves the main driving force for common development," Xi said during the 2024 BRICS summit in Kazan, Russia.
For Xi, development has always been a priority. He sees it as "the master key to solving all problems," and has consistently called for countries worldwide to jointly pursue development and prosperity.
Xi has stressed repeatedly that no one should be left behind in the fight against poverty in China, and has led a formidable campaign that ended extreme poverty nationwide, which was hailed as "the greatest anti-poverty achievement in history."
His "leaving-no-one-behind" conviction also extends to his efforts to support poverty reduction and spur development across the Global South. "On the path to modernization, no one, and no country, should be left behind," Xi said.
Last week in Bishkek, Xi called for consolidating cooperation in both traditional and emerging fields, from trade, investment, connectivity and energy to artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy and green industries.
An aerial photo taken on Oct. 22, 2025 shows wind turbines of De Aar Wind Power Project in De Aar, Northern Cape, South Africa. (Xinhua/Han Xu)
Responding to the Global South's aspirations for common development and modernization, Xi has proposed the Global Development Initiative (GDI), which marks its fifth anniversary this year.
In the last five years, the GDI has mobilized more than 23 billion U.S. dollars, provided support for over 1,800 "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, and sponsored training programs for more than 200,000 people in different professions.
Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper, said: "Under Xi's leadership, the concept of development has acquired a new international dimension and become part of a broader vision for humanity's shared future."
Chinese President Xi Jinping chairs the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" Meeting in Tianjin, north China, Sept. 1, 2025. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen)
GREATER VOICE
As the Global South rises, it deserves a bigger say in global affairs.
Last year's SCO Tianjin summit witnessed Xi's proposal of the Global Governance Initiative, a major proposition of China to advance a more just and equitable global governance system.
At the heart of this vision is the conviction that every country has a place and an equal role to play in global governance.
Xi has long argued that international affairs should not be dictated by those with more muscles. "World affairs should be discussed by all, and international norms should be set by all," he said in Bishkek last week. "The domination of international affairs by a few is an injustice left over from history, and global governance dictated by one, a few or a bloc of countries is not true multilateralism."
"As an important part of a multipolar world and a key driving force behind it, the Global South countries ought to have greater representation and voice in international affairs," Xi said.
Over the years, the SCO and BRICS have grown into vital venues for Global South countries to articulate their interests, coordinate their positions and strengthen their collective influence.
Their growing role can be seen in political coordination. The two groupings have issued statements on international and regional hotspot issues. In March this year, for example, SCO member states issued a statement expressing grave concern over developments in the Middle East and the strikes on Iran.
Xi has also pushed for improving global economic and financial governance. In 2014, Xi and other BRICS leaders formally signed an agreement establishing the New Development Bank, creating a new channel for financing infrastructure and sustainable development in emerging markets and developing countries.
At the SCO Bishkek summit, the members reaffirmed the importance of establishing the SCO Development Bank.
Robotic arms work in an energy storage production workshop at the Sigenergy Nantong Smart Energy Center in Nantong, east China's Jiangsu Province, July 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Yehua)
Now the push for a greater say is extending into emerging areas that will shape the future. In July this year, Xi announced the creation of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, and called for joint efforts to build a just and equitable system of global AI governance.
"We must carry out extensive international cooperation and help Global South countries with capacity building to bridge the AI and digital divides, promote sustainable development, and prevent creating new historical injustice in AI," Xi said.
Beyond the SCO and BRICS, China has also promoted cooperation and greater representation for the Global South through frameworks such as the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation and the China-ASEAN summit.
Xi has said on many occasions that China has always been a member of the Global South and will always belong to the developing world.
"No matter how the international landscape evolves, we in China will always keep the Global South in our heart, and maintain our roots in the Global South," he once said.

item.title: How China drives BRICS expansion and cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Delhi Police personnel stand guard at Pragati Maidan ahead of the upcoming BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, September 6, 2026. /VCG
At the 18th BRICS Summit to be held in New Delhi, India, this upcoming weekend, BRICS has taken on a new meaning. The summit’s theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," also abbreviated as BRICS, highlights the priorities of the organization's new phase of development.
From five countries to 11 members, and from a small group of emerging economies to a platform representing half of the world's population, BRICS has come a long way.
Accounting for 40% of global GDP and with intra-BRICS trade reaching $1.17 trillion in 2024, BRICS has gained considerable weight as it evolves into an increasingly important force in global economics and governance.
China's contribution to BRICS expansion
China has been at the heart of this evolution, especially in promoting inclusiveness and cooperation in BRICS.
At the 2017 Xiamen Summit, China first put forward the "BRICS plus" model, seeking to expand BRICS cooperation to a wider range of emerging economies and amplify the voice of the Global South. Inviting leaders from Egypt, Guinea, Mexico, Tajikistan and Thailand to the summit during its chairmanship, China took the lead in building an open and diversified network of partnerships to boost cooperation on a broader scale.
That proposal soon translated into the membership expansion process. Since then, six new countries, including Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates, have become full members of the organization, culminating in the "Greater BRICS" and a new phase of development that features an enlarged circle of friends.
Following through with its proposal, China has consistently supported BRICS expansion throughout the years. In 2024, BRICS formally established the partner country mechanism, creating a pathway for countries to engage more closely with the bloc without immediately becoming full members. Reaffirming its commitment to an open and inclusive BRICS, China has continued to support more countries in joining the BRICS mechanism, pool the strength of the Global South and build a shared future.
Through its expansion, BRICS will not only help strengthen solidarity and cooperation among developing countries but also enable them to jointly address global economic risks and achieve more stable development, according to a study by Xi Manzhao, a teaching assistant at the School of Northeast Asian Studies, Shandong University, and Yang Yanlong, a research fellow at the Institute of International Studies, Shandong University.
China's solution to global challenges
BRICS's growth is made meaningful through practical measures. To this end, China has also proposed original solutions to common global challenges.
For instance, China has led the establishment of multiple collaborative centers. The China-BRICS Artificial Intelligence Development and Cooperation Center aims to make AI more accessible and affordable for businesses and local governments to solve real, local problems. The BRICS Deep-Sea Resources International Research Center pools research strengths from BRICS nations to tackle resource scarcity and promote equitable, sustainable ocean development. Meanwhile, the China Center for Cooperation on Development of Special Economic Zones in BRICS Countries boosts trade collaboration, policy exchange, and institutional innovation among BRICS nations and emerging markets.
China's contribution not only establishes practical cooperation platforms but also sets up financial mechanisms.
As a founding member of the New Development Bank (NDB), China helped establish a multilateral development bank that provides financing for infrastructure and sustainable development projects. China also pushed for consensus on the Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA), which offers mutual liquidity support and protection from short-term payment pressures, according to a United Nations Trade and Development report.
As BRICS enters a new era with more members and opportunities, China has helped turn the bloc's vision into concrete platforms and mechanisms to address shared development challenges.
Ezzat Saad El Sayed, director of the Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, highlighted China's vital role at the 2025 BRICS summit.
"We cannot imagine what BRICS would look like without China,” he said. “China is a major pillar and a powerful driving force behind BRICS cooperation."

item.title: Pushing in by Land, Water and Air: Expert Explains Extreme Hurdles in Mudslide Rescue
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
A total of 2,141 rescue personnel have been mobilized for search and rescue operations after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Rescue teams are advancing into the hardest-hit core area simultaneously by water, land and air. An expert explained mudslides like this occur under particular terrain and water conditions, and that creates several challenges for rescue teams.
